extra.message: SQL injection in findUserById: the query is built by string concatenation ("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id =" + parameter[0]). parameter[0] is attacker-controlled via req.query.id passed from routes/users/user.js errorBasedSqli (line 28, GET /error-based-sqli?id=) and idorViewProfile (line 205, GET /idor?id=). A payload like id=1 OR 1=1 alters the query; combined with res.send(err) in the route's catch block (user.js:36) this yields error-based SQL injection and full DB extraction.

SQL injection in authenticateUser used for login: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email ='" + parameter[0] + "' AND password = '" + parameter[1] + "'" concatenates the raw username and password from the POST / login form (via passportLocalStrategy.js line 20) directly into the SQL string. A payload such as admin@x'-- or ' OR '1'='1 in the email field bypasses authentication (CWE-287 impact), returning a valid user row that passport logs in.

SQL injection in searchByName: "select id,username,email,fullname,phone from users where username like '%" + username + "%'" concatenates user input directly into the LIKE clause. Reachable from POST /blind-sqli (req.body.username, user.js:54), POST /xss-exercise (user.js:196), GET /second-order-sqli (user.js:79, using the stored req.user.username for second-order SQLi), and POST /blind-sqli-blacklist (user.js:93) where the isFromBlackListOfSqli blacklist in utils/utility.js:36-58 is trivially bypassable (e.g. case variations, inline comments, since the regexes are unanchored and case-sensitive). Payload example: x%' OR '1'='1.

OS command injection in pingMe: let command = 'ping -c 3 ' + ip; followed by exec(command, ...). The ip value comes from req.body.ip via POST /command-injection (routes/users/user.js:135 -> usersController.commandInjection). Because the input is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, a payload such as 127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd or `id` executes arbitrary commands on the server with the application's privileges (remote code execution).

Path traversal / arbitrary file read in readDosAndDonts: filePath = path.join(__dirname, filename); fs.readFile(filePath, ...). filename is attacker-controlled via req.query.filename from GET /arbitrary-file-retrieval (routes/users/user.js:144). path.join does not sanitize ../ sequences, so a request like /arbitrary-file-retrieval?filename=../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files outside the intended directory (file contents are then rendered in the page via arbitrary-file-retrieval.ejs line 44).

XML External Entity (XXE) injection in parseXML: libxmljs parseXmlString is called with parserOptions { noent: true } which enables entity expansion/substitution. The XML comes from req.body.search via POST /xxe (routes/users/user.js:168, usersController.xxe). A crafted payload like <?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><user>&xxe;</user> causes the server to read local files (and could be used for SSRF) whose contents are returned in the response.

Insecure deserialization leading to remote code execution in getDeserializeData: the base64-encoded 'user' cookie (fully attacker-controlled, set unsigned via res.cookie in routes/users/user.js:244 and readable/writable by the client) is decoded and passed to node-serialize's unserialize() without any validation. node-serialize evaluates the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ IIFE marker during deserialization, so a cookie containing {"fullname":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function (){ require('child_process').execSync('...'); }()"} executes arbitrary code on the server (the exact RCE payload is even documented in the code comment at controllers/usersController.js:202). Exposed via GET /deserialization (user.js:177).

Regex injection / ReDoS in searchLogs: let rgx = new RegExp('(public\\[\\d+\\] +.*' + search + '.*)') embeds req.body.search (from POST /regex-injection, routes/users/user.js:156) directly into a RegExp. Attackers can break out of the intended pattern with input like )|(.* (changing matching semantics to return all lines) or supply nested quantifiers (e.g. .*.*.*.*.*.*.*) causing catastrophic backtracking on every line of the log file, blocking the Node.js event loop (denial of service).

Reflected XSS with insufficient sanitization in searchByName: htmlResponse = "

User " + custom_sanitizer_regex(username) + " not present". The custom_sanitizer_regex function (utils/utility.js:2-12) performs a single, non-global replacement of the pattern <(\\w+)\\W+[\\w] which is trivially bypassable (the code comment itself documents the bypass <alert(1)). The resulting HTML is rendered unescaped via <%- htmlResponse %> in views/blind-sqli.ejs:65 and views/xss-exercise.ejs:67, so req.body.username from POST /blind-sqli executes in the victim's browser.

Reflected XSS in searchUserBlackList: htmlResponse = "

User " + username + " not present" concatenates req.body.username with no HTML encoding at all (the isFromBlackListOfSqli check only screens SQL keywords). The string is rendered unescaped via <%- htmlResponse %> in views/reflected-xss.ejs:65 and views/blind-sqli-blacklist.ejs:65, so any payload not matching the SQL blacklist (e.g. ipt>alert(1) or

) executes in the browser of anyone submitting or viewing the search result.

Reflected XSS in the xxe() controller method: htmlResponse = "

User " + username + " not present" where username is the entity-expanded value extracted from attacker-supplied XML (req.body.search via POST /xxe). The value is embedded into HTML with no encoding and the response is sent raw via res.send(htmlResponse) (routes/users/user.js:170) and inserted into the DOM with jQuery .html() in views/xxe.ejs:100, allowing script execution in the victim's browser.

Stored XSS in generateSearchUserResponse: database values user[i].fullname, user[i].username, user[i].email and user[i].phone (lines 232-235) are concatenated directly into an HTML table. These fields are stored unvalidated via the public POST /register endpoint (models/usersModel.js registerUser insert), and the isFromBlackListOfXSS blacklist (utils/utility.js:14-34) is bypassable (it omits tags such as <details>, <marquee>, <form> and handlers such as onerror/ontoggle/onfocus). Any authenticated user searching for the stored value (e.g. via /blind-sqli, /reflected-xss, /second-order-sqli) gets the payload rendered unescaped through <%- htmlResponse %>.

Stored XSS via unescaped EJS output: <%- fullName %> at views/body-header.ejs lines 34 and 42, and <%- fullName %> at views/navigation.ejs line 17, render the user's fullname from the database without HTML encoding. fullname is attacker-controlled through the public registration form (POST /register stores it raw), so registering with a fullname like executes script on every authenticated page that includes the header/navigation partials (also enabling session/cookie theft since the session cookie is set httpOnly:false in app.js:28).

DOM-based XSS: the inline script reads the URL query parameter via getUrlVars()["default"] (helper defined in views/header.ejs:18-24) and writes it into the document with document.write("") without any encoding. Navigating to any page with ?default= (URL-encoded) executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the context of the authenticated page (see views/dom-xss.ejs which documents this exercise).

XSS via deserialized cookie value in the deserialization() controller method: resolve("

Hi," + fullname + "


") embeds the fullname extracted from the attacker-controlled base64 'user' cookie into HTML without encoding; it is rendered unescaped via <%- htmlResponse %> in views/deserialization.ejs:44. Setting the cookie to base64({"fullname":""}) executes script in the victim's browser.

IDOR (insecure direct object reference) in errorBasedSqli: getUser(req.query.id) fetches and displays the profile of any user (fullname, email, phone, username are rendered into the form in views/error-based-sqli.ejs:55-70) using the attacker-supplied id parameter, with no ownership check against the authenticated session user (req.user.id). Changing ?id=2, ?id=3, ... leaks other users' personal data.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IDOR / broken access control in updateProfile (POST /update-profile): usersController.updateUserById(req.body, req.query.id) uses the attacker-controlled query-string id to select which user record to update (models/usersModel.js updateUserById 'update users set ... where id=?') instead of the session user's id. Any authenticated user can modify the fullname, username, email and phone of any other user by sending ?id=<victim_id>, and the response redirects to /error-based-sqli?id=<victim_id> (line 43).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IDOR in idorViewProfile (GET /idor): getUser(req.query.id) loads an arbitrary user's profile (rendered in views/idor.ejs:55-70) based solely on the user-supplied id parameter with no authorization check that the requested id matches the authenticated session user, exposing other users' email, phone, fullname and username.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IDOR / broken access control in idorUpdateProfile (POST /idor): usersController.updateUserById(req.body, req.query.id) updates whichever user record the attacker chooses via the ?id= query parameter, with no verification that the target id belongs to the authenticated session user. Any logged-in user can overwrite another user's profile details.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Insecure password change (POST /change-password): usersController.changePassword(req.body.password, req.body.id) takes BOTH the new password and the target user id from the request body (the id comes from a spoofable hidden form field, views/change-password.ejs:51) without verifying the current password or that the id matches the authenticated session user. Any authenticated user can change any other user's password (models/usersModel.js changePassword: 'update users set password=? where id=?'), resulting in full account takeover of arbitrary accounts.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Missing CSRF protection: the csurf package is declared in package.json but is never imported or mounted anywhere in the application. All state-changing endpoints mounted at app.use('/', indexRouter) — POST / (login), POST /register, POST /update-profile, POST /blind-sqli, POST /reflected-xss, POST /xss-exercise, POST /change-password, POST /command-injection, POST /regex-injection, POST /xxe and POST /idor — accept cookie-session-authenticated requests with no anti-CSRF token or same-origin check, allowing an attacker site to forge requests in a victim's browser (e.g. silently changing the victim's password via POST /change-password).

Hardcoded, publicly-known express-session secret: secret: 'secrettobechanged'. Anyone who knows this value (it is committed to the repository) can forge valid signed session cookies (connect.sid), impersonating any user or elevating privileges by setting the session to an arbitrary user id, since passport.deserializeUser trusts the id stored in the session (utils/passportLocalStrategy.js:10-16).

Insecure session cookie configuration: cookie: { httpOnly: false, secure: false }. httpOnly:false allows JavaScript (including any injected via the multiple XSS flaws) to read the connect.sid session cookie and hijack the session; secure:false causes the session cookie to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP where it can be intercepted.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Flag

extra.message: Session fixation risk: the session is created with saveUninitialized: true (a session cookie is issued on the unauthenticated login page before login) and the session identifier is never regenerated on successful authentication (req.logIn in routes/users/user.js:13 does not call req.session.regenerate). An attacker who fixes a known session id on a victim's browser retains a valid session after the victim logs in, enabling session hijacking (this is exactly the exercise documented in views/session-mgmt.ejs).

Plaintext password storage: registerUser inserts user.password directly into the users table with no hashing or salting (the sha512 helper in utils/sha512.js is available but never used for registration or authentication), and authenticateUser (models/usersModel.js:15) compares the plaintext password directly in the SQL query. A database compromise exposes every user's password in cleartext, and password reuse makes this critical.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password
CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Sensitive error disclosure: return res.send(err) serializes the raw error object — including full MySQL error messages, SQL fragments and stack traces — directly into the HTTP response. The same pattern appears at routes/users/user.js lines 45, 213 and 222 (updateProfile, idorViewProfile, idorUpdateProfile). Combined with the SQL injection in findUserById this exposes internal database structure and query details to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded default database credentials: when the DATABASE_USER / DATABASE_PASS environment variables are unset, the application falls back to connecting with the hardcoded credentials "user" / "pass" (lines 4-5). Deployments that omit these variables silently run with well-known, committed credentials.
